arxiv-1612-00690.title: A Bayesian Heteroscedastic GLM with Application to fMRI Data with Motion Spikes
arxiv-1612-00690.creator: Anders Eklund, Martin A. Lindquist, Mattias Villani*
arxiv-1612-00690.description: Abstract We propose a voxel-wise general linear model with autoregressive noise and heteroscedastic noise innovations (GLMH) for analyzing functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data. The model is analyzed from a Bayesian perspective and has the benefit of automatically down-weighting time points close to motion spikes in a data-driven manner.

arxiv-2010-09425.title: Synthesizing the Unseen for Zero-shot Object Detection
arxiv-2010-09425.creator: Nasir Hayat, Munawar Hayat, Shafin Rahman, Salman Khan, Syed Waqas Zamir, Fahad Shahbaz Khan
arxiv-2010-09425.description: Abstract The existing zero-shot detection approaches project visual features to the semantic domain for seen objects, hoping to map unseen objects to their corresponding semantics during inference. However, since the unseen objects are never visualized during training, the detection model is skewed towards seen content, thereby labeling unseen as background or a seen class.

Time-of-flight (TOF) cameras are sensors that can measure the depths of scene-points, by illuminating the scene with a controlled laser or LED source, and then analyzing the reflected light.

arxiv-2402-13364.title: A Simple but Effective Approach to Improve Structured Language Model Output for Information Extraction
arxiv-2402-13364.creator: Yinghao Li, Rampi Ramprasad, Chao Zhang, rampi.ramprasad@mse.gatech.edu
arxiv-2402-13364.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive abilities in generating unstructured natural language according to instructions. However, their performance can be inconsistent when tasked with producing text that adheres to specific structured formats, which is crucial in applications like named entity recognition (NER) or relation extraction (RE).

arxiv-2412-06138.title: SGIA: Enhancing Fine-Grained Visual Classification with Sequence Generative Image Augmentation
arxiv-2412-06138.creator: Qiyu Liao, Xin Yuan, Min Xu, Dadong Wang
arxiv-2412-06138.description: Abstract In Fine-Grained Visual Classification (FGVC), distinguishing highly similar subcategories remains a formidable challenge, often necessitating datasets with extensive variability. The acquisition and annotation of such FGVC datasets are notably difficult and costly, demanding specialized knowledge to identify subtle distinctions among closely related categories.

arxiv-2509-10064.title: From customer survey feedback to software improvements: Leveraging the full potential of data 2023 From customer survey feedback to software improvements: Leveraging the full potential of data – References
arxiv-2509-10064.creator: Erik Bertram, Nina Hollender, Sebastian Juhl, Sandra Loop, Martin Schrepp
arxiv-2509-10064.description: Abstract Converting customer survey feedback data into usable insights has always been a great challenge for large software enterprises. Despite the improvements on this field, a major obstacle often remains when drawing the right conclusions out of the data and channeling them into the software development process.

arxiv-2510-04665.title: Interactive High-Performance Visualization for Astronomy and Cosmology
arxiv-2510-04665.creator: Eva Sciacca 1 5 , Nicola Tuccari 2 1 5 , Umer Arshad 3 5 , Fabio Pitari 4 , Giuseppa Muscianisi 4 , Emiliano Tramontana 2
arxiv-2510-04665.description: Abstract The exponential growth of data in Astrophysics and Cosmology demands scalable computational tools and intuitive interfaces for analysis and visualization. In this work, we present an innovative integration of the VisIVO scientific visualization framework with the InterActive Computing (IAC) service at Cineca, enabling interactive, high-performance visual workflows directly within HPC environments.

arxiv-2510-17988.title: First-passage properties of the jump process with a drift. The general case
arxiv-2510-17988.creator: Ivan N. Burenev
arxiv-2510-17988.description: Abstract . We study the first-passage properties of a jump process with constant drift where jump amplitudes and inter-arrival times follow arbitrary light-tailed distributions with smooth densities. Using a mapping to an effective discrete-time random walk, we identify three regimes determined by the drift strength: survival (weak drift), absorption (strong drift), and critical.

pmc-11470683.title: Spinster homolog 2 (SPNS2) deficiency drives endothelial cell senescence and vascular aging via promoting pyruvate metabolism mediated mitochondrial dysfunction
pmc-11470683.creator: Haojun Tang, Pan Gao, Weng Peng, Xiaodan Wang, Zhenbo Wang, Weiqian Deng, Kai Yin, Xiao Zhu
pmc-11470683.description: Endothelial cell (EC) senescence and vascular aging are important hallmarks of chronic metabolic diseases. An improved understanding of the precise regulation of EC senescence may provide novel therapeutic strategies for EC and vascular aging-related diseases. This study examined the potential functions of Spinster homolog 2 (SPNS2) in EC senescence and vascular aging.

pmc-12799064.title: Intragastric Ectopic Liver
pmc-12799064.creator: Jessy Fadel, Philippe Attieh, Karam Karam, Paul Rassam, Zarouhie Meguerian, Elias Fiani, Ihab I. El Hajj
pmc-12799064.description: BackgroundEctopic liver (EL) is a rare developmental anomaly defined as hepatic tissue located outside the native liver without vascular or biliary continuity. It is most commonly reported in the gallbladder but has also been described in other intra-abdominal and extra-abdominal sites. The gastric location is exceptionally rare, with only a handful of cases reported in the literature.

pmc-13117151.title: Beyond the Usual Suspects: IgG4-Related Disease as a Rare Culprit in Cardiac Valvular Disorders
pmc-13117151.creator: Piera Costanzo, Savino Sciascia, Giacomo Quattrocchio, Pierluigi Sbarra, Antonella Barreca, Roberta Bracci, Irene Cecchi, Massimo Radin, Elisa Menegatti, Simone Baldovino
pmc-13117151.description: Cardiologists consider degenerative or infectious causes when evaluating valvular heart disease. However, the role of autoimmune disorders, though less frequent, remains clinically significant. This report describes a young male patient presenting with persistent coronary disease and a suspected valvular cusp perforation initially attributed to infective endocarditis, which ultimately proved to be a manifestation of IgG4-related disease.
